A grommet is seated by hand over a cut panel edge. We specify hardness and tear strength for that moment, not just for service life — a part the operator has to force is a part that gets damaged on the line.
Each hole is moulded undersize against its wire. Send the wire diameters and we will set the interference — matching hole to wire exactly gives a grommet that passes inspection and leaks in service.
Sized to your panel, not to a catalogue
Panel gauge sets the retaining groove; hole pitch is fixed by your harness. Both are moulded in, so the part seats in one push and stays put.
Protecting the cable is half the job
A chafed harness is a short circuit, so the bore is moulded with a radius rather than cut, and the compound is chosen to stay flexible cold.
Bulkhead and floor-pan harness pass-throughs, door-to-body cable transitions, lamp and switch wiring
Control panels, junction boxes and outdoor cabinets, where the grommet is what carries the enclosure’s IP rating under IEC 60529
Harness entries on machine enclosures and control cabinets, where dust and washdown are the threats
Cable entries on roadside cabinets, pump housings and site equipment
Polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. Tear strength is set here — the grommet is stretched over a cut panel edge by hand, and that moment decides line scrap.
Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. The retaining groove and the three cores are cut to your panel gauge and hole pitch.
Hydraulic press cycles at controlled temperature and pressure profiles per product spec.
Flash removed from the three bores and the groove. Flash left in a bore is a leak path and a chafe point.
Hole diameters, pitch and groove dimension checked against the drawing, plus hardness testing and batch sampling.
Industrial packing with documentation. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used. Grommets are bagged loose so the sealing lips are not deformed in transit.

Dimensioned drawings and 3D models are issued on request, under NDA where required. Send the panel gauge, hole diameter and the three wire sizes — or a sample and a panel offcut — and we will return a drawing for approval.
What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes. Send the sample and a piece of the panel it fits. The groove has to match the panel gauge, and a used grommet has relaxed — we measure the panel, not the worn part, and set the hole interference from your wire sizes.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?
PDF, DWG, DXF and STEP. Mark the panel gauge, the panel hole diameter, the three wire diameters and the hole pitch — those four, plus the compound, are enough for us to quote and tool.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412, compression set to ASTM D395 Method B and tear strength to ASTM D624 are tested in-house.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?
TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment.
